item.title: ERCache: Efficient Caching Framework for Large-Scale User Representations in Meta's Ads System
item.description:
Meta deployed ERCache, an efficient and reliable caching framework for large-scale user representations in their ads system, running in production for over six months supporting more than 30 ranking models.

The key insight came from analyzing user access patterns at Meta: most user model inferences occur within a short timeframe. This revealed a triangular relationship among model complexity, embedding freshness, and service SLAs. ERCache exploits this by splitting cache into direct and failover types with customized settings and eviction policies for each model.

The framework questions whether user model inference is necessary for every ad request in large-scale social networks. By caching user representations intelligently, ERCache reduces computational costs while maintaining embedding freshness within acceptable bounds. The system balances model complexity, embedding freshness, and SLAs while accounting for staleness introduced by caching.

This work addresses a practical challenge that every large-scale ad system faces: as models grow more complex, the computational cost of generating user representations for every request becomes prohibitive. ERCache's approach of model-aware caching with staleness management offers a production-validated solution that has been running at Meta scale for months.

Sources:

  • https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06497

item.title: LiRank: Industrial Large Scale Ranking Models at LinkedIn with Residual DCN Architecture
item.description:
LinkedIn published LiRank, their industrial-scale ranking framework deployed across Feed ranking, Jobs recommendations, and Ads CTR prediction. The results: +0.5% member sessions for Feed, +1.76% qualified job applications for Jobs, and +4.3% CTR improvement for Ads.

The core architectural contribution is Residual DCN, which adds attention and residual connections to the DCNv2 architecture. LiRank combines this with dense gating, transformers, and model compression techniques including quantization and vocabulary compression to create a unified ranking framework.

Key technical contributions include novel calibration techniques and productionized deep learning-based explore/exploit methods. The framework was designed to serve multiple products from a single codebase, enabling shared infrastructure and technique propagation across LinkedIn's ranking surfaces.

LiRank is significant because it demonstrates that a single ranking framework can deliver improvements across diverse product surfaces (Feed, Jobs, Ads) with different optimization objectives. The Residual DCN architecture and the production engineering around it represent LinkedIn's approach to scaling ranking models across their platform.

Sources:

  • https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.06859

item.title: GRAB: Generative Ranking for Ads at Baidu with LLM-Inspired Sequence-First CTR Prediction
item.description:
Baidu deployed GRAB (Generative Ranking for Ads at Baidu), an end-to-end generative CTR prediction model inspired by LLM scaling principles. In full-scale online deployment, GRAB achieved +3.05% revenue and +3.49% CTR over established DLRM baselines in production.

The core innovation is the Causal Action-aware Multi-channel Attention (CamA) mechanism, which captures temporal dynamics and specific action signals in user behavior sequences. Unlike traditional Deep Learning Recommendation Models (DLRMs) that struggle with generalization and long-sequence modeling, GRAB treats recommendation as a sequence modeling problem analogous to language modeling — a "sequence-first" paradigm.

The CamA mechanism handles multi-channel user behavior sequences with causal (action-aware) attention, enabling the model to process long interaction histories effectively. This is critical because user behavior in advertising involves multiple types of actions (views, clicks, conversions) across different channels, and the temporal relationships between these actions contain important signal for predicting future engagement.

One of the most significant findings is the scaling behavior: GRAB reports monotonic and approximately linear improvement in expressive power as longer interaction sequences are used, mirroring the scaling laws observed in LLMs. This suggests that the same principles driving progress in language modeling — more data, longer context, larger models — can be applied to ad ranking systems.

The paper positions GRAB as a replacement for traditional DLRM architectures that have dominated ad tech for years. While DLRMs use embedding tables and feature interaction modules, GRAB's generative approach processes user behavior as a sequence, potentially capturing more complex patterns in user intent evolution.

For ad tech practitioners, this work demonstrates that the LLM paradigm can deliver concrete revenue and CTR improvements in production ad systems. The scaling law finding is particularly important because it provides a principled way to predict how model improvements will translate to business outcomes as more user history is incorporated.

The deployment at Baidu — one of the largest advertising platforms in China — validates that these techniques work at true industrial scale, not just in research settings. The 3%+ revenue lift from a single model change is substantial by industry standards.

Sources:

  • https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.01865

item.title: ML-DCN: Masked Low-Rank Deep Crossing Network for Scalable Ads CTR Prediction at Pinterest
item.description:
Pinterest published ML-DCN (Masked Low-Rank Deep Crossing Network), a feature interaction module that combines DCNv2 and MaskNet into a unified architecture for their ads ranking system. The key finding: naively scaling DCNv2 and MaskNet yields rapidly diminishing offline gains, but ML-DCN achieves higher AUC than both at matched FLOPs with a more favorable AUC-FLOPs trade-off.

The architecture integrates an instance-conditioned mask into a low-rank crossing layer. This enables per-example selection where the mask is conditioned on each individual input instance, allowing dynamic, sample-level feature interaction filtering. The mechanism amplifies salient interaction directions while maintaining efficient computation through low-rank decomposition.

The motivation comes from a practical production constraint: ad ranking models must respect strict latency and FLOPs budgets during serving. As models grow larger, the marginal accuracy gains per additional FLOP decrease. ML-DCN addresses this by being smarter about how it uses compute rather than simply adding more parameters.

In online A/B testing, ML-DCN demonstrated statistically significant improvements in key ads metrics including CTR and click-quality measures. Critically, it was deployed in Pinterest's production system with neutral serving cost — meaning the accuracy gains came without additional computational overhead.

This work is significant because it addresses the scaling problem that every production ad system faces: how to continue improving model accuracy when you're already at the latency/compute ceiling. ML-DCN's approach of combining masking (for dynamic feature selection) with low-rank decomposition (for efficient computation) offers a practical solution that has been validated in Pinterest's production ads system.

The paper also highlights an important methodological point: evaluating models at matched FLOPs rather than just comparing raw accuracy. This AUC-FLOPs Pareto frontier analysis is more meaningful for production systems where compute budgets are fixed.

Sources:

  • https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09194

item.title: CAN: Feature Co-Action Network for CTR Prediction at Alibaba with 12% CTR and 8% RPM Lift
item.description:
Alibaba deployed the Co-Action Network (CAN) for CTR prediction in their display advertisement system, achieving +12% CTR improvement and +8% RPM (Revenue Per Mille) improvement in production. The paper was published at WSDM 2022.

The core insight is that DNN-based implicit interaction learning cannot fully retain the complete representation capacity of original and empirical feature interactions. Even simple cartesian product features outperform FM-based implicit interaction models. CAN addresses this by modeling pairwise feature interactions using two learned components: Feature A's embedding and Feature B's MLP. The interaction is computed by passing the embedding of Feature A through the MLP network of Feature B — a mechanism termed "feature co-action."

This approach approximates explicit pairwise interactions (like cartesian products) without the parameter explosion that makes cartesian products impractical at scale. CAN provides a powerful capacity for fitting complex feature interactions while avoiding the high parameter cost of explicit representations.

The 12% CTR lift and 8% RPM improvement in Alibaba's production display advertising system are substantial numbers. For context, a 1% CTR improvement at Alibaba's scale translates to significant revenue. An 8% RPM improvement means the system is generating more revenue per thousand impressions, benefiting both the platform and advertisers.

CAN outperforms state-of-the-art CTR models and the cartesian product baseline on both public and industrial datasets. The key advantage is that it captures the expressiveness of explicit feature interactions while maintaining the parameter efficiency of implicit methods.

For practitioners, CAN demonstrates that the feature interaction problem in CTR prediction hasn't been fully solved by existing approaches like DCN, DeepFM, or xDeepFM. The co-action mechanism — where one feature's embedding is transformed through another feature's MLP — is a simple but effective way to model complex feature dependencies that are missed by inner product or element-wise product interactions.

The deployment at Alibaba's display advertising system, one of the largest in the world, validates that these techniques work at true industrial scale with meaningful business impact.

Sources:

  • https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.05625

item.title: DHEN: Deep Hierarchical Ensemble Network for Ad CVR Prediction at Pinterest (WWW 2025)
item.description:
Pinterest published their experience deploying DHEN (Deep Hierarchical Ensemble Network) for conversion ad CVR prediction, accepted at WWW 2025. The model integrates multiple feature crossing modules — MLP, DCN, Transformer, and potentially others — into a single backbone architecture to predict all CVR tasks.

The paper addresses three key architecture challenges: which feature-crossing modules to include, how deep and wide to set DHEN for the best trade-off between efficiency and efficacy, and hyper-parameter selection for each module. These are practical questions that every production ad system faces when designing ensemble architectures.

DHEN builds two types of behavioral sequences: on-site real-time user behavior sequences and off-site conversion event sequences. The off-site data captures user actions on third-party websites or apps (purchases, add-to-cart, sign-ups), providing richer signal for conversion prediction than on-site clicks alone.

A key contribution is a self-supervised auxiliary loss to address label sparsity in CVR prediction. Conversion events are inherently rare compared to clicks, making CVR prediction significantly harder than CTR prediction. The auxiliary loss predicts future actions in the input sequence, providing additional training signal that helps the model learn better representations.

The multitask learning framework uses DHEN as the single backbone model to predict all CVR tasks, achieving state-of-the-art performance compared to previous single feature crossing modules with pre-trained user personalization features.

This work is significant because CVR prediction is one of the most challenging problems in ad tech. The combination of hierarchical ensemble architecture, off-site conversion data, and self-supervised auxiliary losses addresses multiple aspects of the CVR prediction problem simultaneously. The deployment at Pinterest's conversion ads system validates that these techniques deliver real business impact.

For practitioners, DHEN demonstrates that carefully designed ensemble architectures with multiple feature crossing modules can outperform individual modules, but the design choices (which modules, how deep, what hyperparameters) require systematic experimentation. The self-supervised auxiliary loss for handling label sparsity is a technique that could be applied to other sparse prediction tasks in ad tech.

Sources:

  • https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.08169

item.title: Entity Representation Learning Through Onsite-Offsite Graph for Pinterest Ads: 2.69% CTR Lift
item.description:
Pinterest deployed an entity representation learning system using onsite-offsite graphs for their ads engagement model, achieving 2.69% CTR lift and 1.34% CPC reduction in production. The system builds a large-scale heterogeneous graph from users' onsite ad interactions and opt-in offsite conversion activities.

The core challenge was that Ads ranking models initially struggled to directly incorporate Knowledge Graph Embeddings (KGE), with only modest gains observed during offline experiments. The paper introduces TransRA (TransR with Anchors), a novel KGE model designed specifically for integrating graph embeddings into ads ranking models.

Two key techniques make this work: a Large ID Embedding Table technique to handle the scale of Pinterest's entity graph, and an attention-based KGE finetuning approach within the ads ranking models. The attention mechanism allows the ranking model to selectively focus on the most relevant graph-derived features for each prediction.

The graph connects two types of user activity: onsite ad interactions (within Pinterest) and offsite conversion activities (opt-in data capturing shopping interest on external sites). This dual-source approach captures both explicit engagement signals and implicit purchase intent, providing richer entity representations than either source alone.

The system builds on GNN approaches including GraphSage, TwHIM, and LiGNN, which construct graphs from user platform activities. However, the key innovation is the integration method — how to effectively use graph-derived embeddings in a production ranking model without degrading serving performance.

The 2.69% CTR lift and 1.34% CPC reduction demonstrate that entity-level graph features can deliver meaningful improvements in ad ranking. The CPC reduction is particularly valuable because it means advertisers pay less per click while the system maintains or improves click rates — a win for both sides of the marketplace.

For practitioners, this work highlights the potential of combining onsite and offsite user data through graph-based representations. The challenge is in the integration — simply adding graph embeddings to a ranking model doesn't work well. Pinterest's attention-based finetuning approach provides a practical solution that has been validated at production scale.

Sources:

  • https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.02609

item.title: MSD: LLM-Infused CTR Prediction via Knowledge Distillation at Meituan (WWW 2025)
item.description:
Meituan deployed MSD (Multi-level Deep Semantic Information Infused CTR model via Distillation), a framework that distills knowledge from large language models into smaller, more efficient CTR prediction models. The system was validated through online A/B tests on Meituan's sponsored-search system, significantly outperforming baseline models in terms of Cost Per Mile (CPM) and CTR. The paper was accepted at WWW 2025.

The core challenge MSD addresses is how to leverage the deep semantic understanding capabilities of LLMs for CTR prediction without incurring the computational cost of running LLMs at inference time. LLMs have "comprehensive world knowledge capabilities" that can enrich feature representations, but they are too slow for real-time ad serving.

MSD uses a knowledge distillation pipeline where LLMs extract and distill deep semantic insights into a smaller model. The distilled model captures multi-level semantic information at both user and item levels — semantic modeling that traditional approaches often overlook. The system operates end-to-end, meaning the distilled model runs seamlessly at serving time without any LLM dependency.

The framework is designed to balance efficiency and effectiveness, aiming for high predictive performance while maintaining optimal resource utilization. This is critical for sponsored search, where latency requirements are strict (typically under 10ms for the ranking model) and traffic volume is enormous.

MSD was deployed on Meituan's sponsored-search system, one of the largest food delivery and local services platforms in China. The online A/B test results showing significant CPM and CTR improvements validate that LLM-derived knowledge can improve production ad systems when properly distilled.

For practitioners, MSD demonstrates a practical pattern for incorporating LLM knowledge into production ad systems: use LLMs during training to enrich feature representations, then distill that knowledge into lightweight models that can serve in real-time. This avoids the latency and cost issues of running LLMs at inference time while still benefiting from their semantic understanding capabilities.

The multi-level semantic modeling — capturing semantics at both user and item levels — is an important design choice. Traditional CTR models often treat semantic features as flat embeddings, losing the hierarchical structure that LLMs can capture. MSD's approach of distilling this hierarchical semantic knowledge offers a way to bridge the gap between LLM capabilities and production ad system requirements.

Sources:

  • https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06860

item.title: DUAL: Deep Uncertainty-Aware Learning for Online Advertising at Alibaba with 8% Revenue Lift
item.description:
Alibaba deployed DUAL (Deep Uncertainty-Aware Learning) for their display advertising platform, achieving 8.2% social welfare improvement and 8.0% revenue lift in online A/B testing. The paper was published at SIGKDD 2021.

DUAL combines Gaussian processes with deep neural networks for CTR prediction with uncertainty estimation. The key innovation is learning CTR models based on Gaussian processes, which can provide predictive uncertainty estimations while maintaining the flexibility of deep neural networks. This uncertainty information is then linked to well-known bandit algorithms for ad ranking.

The method can be easily implemented on existing models and deployed in real-time systems with minimal extra computational overhead. This is a critical practical requirement — any uncertainty estimation method that significantly increases serving latency or complexity would not be viable in production ad systems.

DUAL-based ad-ranking strategies are designed to boost long-term utilities such as social welfare in advertising systems, addressing the exploration-exploitation trade-off via contextual bandits. The uncertainty estimates help the system balance between exploiting known good ads and exploring potentially better alternatives.

The 8.2% social welfare improvement and 8.0% revenue lift are substantial numbers. Social welfare in advertising refers to the overall value created for all participants — advertisers, users, and the platform. Improving social welfare means the system is making better matches between ads and users, benefiting everyone.

The exploration-exploitation trade-off is fundamental to ad systems: showing only the highest-predicted-CTR ads leads to over-exploitation and missed opportunities, while too much exploration wastes ad inventory on potentially poor ads. DUAL's uncertainty-aware approach provides a principled way to balance this trade-off.

For practitioners, DUAL demonstrates that uncertainty estimation can deliver concrete business improvements in production ad systems. The approach is model-agnostic — it can be added to existing CTR models without major architectural changes. The key insight is that knowing how confident the model is in its predictions is as valuable as the predictions themselves for making better ranking decisions.

The deployment at Alibaba's display advertising platform, one of the world's largest, validates that uncertainty-aware learning works at true industrial scale with meaningful business impact.

Sources:

  • https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.02298

item.title: TwERC: High Performance Ensembled Candidate Generation for Ads Recommendation at Twitter
item.description:
Twitter deployed TwERC, a machine learning-first heterogeneous re-architecture of the candidate generation stage for their large-scale ads recommendation system. The system achieved 4.08% revenue gain from graph-based similarity sourcing and 1.38% revenue gain from rankscore caching, with the two strategies complementing each other.

Modern recommendation systems split into two stages: candidate generation and heavy ranking, balancing computational cost against recommendation quality. TwERC focuses on the candidate generation phase, which selects a broad set of potentially relevant ads from the full inventory before the more expensive ranking stage evaluates them.

The core design combines a real-time light ranker with two sourcing strategies that capture additional information the base ranker misses:

  • Graph-based Similarity: Uses a notion of similarity in the interaction graph to source additional candidates, achieving 4.08% revenue gain. This captures collaborative filtering signals that pointwise models miss.
  • Rankscore Caching: Caches previous scores from the ranking stage to feed back into candidate generation, achieving 1.38% revenue gain. This leverages expensive ranking computations across requests.

The key insight is that the two strategies have biases that complement both the light ranker and one another. The graph-based approach captures structural relationships in user-ad interactions, while the caching approach captures temporal patterns in ad relevance. Together, they provide broader coverage than either alone.

The paper also describes a set of metrics for understanding the complex product trade-offs inherent in industrial candidate generation systems. These metrics help evaluate not just accuracy but also diversity, coverage, and freshness of the candidate set.

For practitioners, TwERC demonstrates that the candidate generation stage — often overlooked in favor of the ranking stage — offers significant optimization opportunities. The combination of a real-time light ranker with complementary sourcing strategies is a practical architecture that can deliver meaningful revenue improvements.

The deployment at Twitter's ads system validates that these techniques work at scale. The total revenue gain from both strategies (5.46% combined) is substantial by industry standards, demonstrating that investing in candidate generation quality pays off.

Sources:

  • https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.13915

item.title: DeepLight: Deep Lightweight Feature Interactions for 46X Speedup in Ad Serving (WSDM 2021)
item.description:
Researchers from Twitter published DeepLight, a framework that accelerates CTR prediction through three optimization techniques, achieving 46X speedup on Criteo and 27X speedup on Avazu without any loss in prediction accuracy. The paper was accepted at WSDM 2021.

DeepLight addresses the fundamental tension between model complexity and serving latency in ad systems. Embedding-based neural networks that combine a shallow component (for explicit feature interactions) and a deep neural network component (for deep feature interactions) can slow down prediction inference by hundreds of times in production ad serving.

Three key mechanisms enable the speedup:

  • Shallow Component Optimization: Accelerates model inference by explicitly searching informative feature interactions in the shallow component, eliminating redundant computations.
  • DNN Component Compression: Prunes redundant layers and parameters at both intra-layer and inter-layer levels in the DNN component, reducing model size and computation.
  • Embedding Sparsity: Promotes the sparsity of the embedding layer to preserve the most discriminant signals while eliminating noise.

The 46X speedup on Criteo without accuracy loss is remarkable. In production ad systems, latency directly impacts revenue — every millisecond of additional latency reduces user engagement and ad impressions. A 46X speedup means the model can either serve more traffic with the same hardware or use more complex features within the same latency budget.

The approach is particularly relevant for ad systems that need to serve millions of requests per second with strict latency SLAs (typically 10-50ms end-to-end). By compressing the model without losing accuracy, DeepLight enables more sophisticated models to be deployed within existing infrastructure constraints.

For practitioners, DeepLight demonstrates that significant speedups are possible through systematic model compression without retraining. The three-pronged approach — optimizing the shallow component, compressing the DNN, and promoting embedding sparsity — addresses different sources of computational overhead simultaneously.

The code is open-sourced on GitHub, making it accessible for practitioners who want to apply these techniques to their own ad systems.

Sources:

  • https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.06987

item.title: CowClip: Reducing CTR Prediction Training Time from 12 Hours to 10 Minutes on 1 GPU (AAAI 2023)
item.description:
ByteDance published CowClip (Adaptive Column-wise Clipping), a technique that enables 128X batch size scaling in CTR prediction model training with no accuracy loss. On DeepFM with the Criteo dataset, training time was reduced from 12 hours to 10 minutes on a single V100 GPU, with over 0.1% AUC improvement. The paper was accepted at AAAI 2023.

The core problem is that CTR prediction models are trained on massive daily data volumes, making training slow and expensive. Large batch training could accelerate this, but previous scaling rules fail in the training of CTR prediction neural networks. The authors theoretically show that different frequencies of feature IDs make it challenging to scale hyperparameters when scaling the batch size.

CowClip addresses this by enabling an easy and effective scaling rule for the embeddings: keep the learning rate unchanged while scaling the L2 loss. This stabilizes training under large batch size settings, preventing the divergence that typically occurs when batch sizes are increased naively.

The technique was applied across four CTR prediction networks (including DeepFM) and tested on two real-world datasets. The results show that batch size can be enlarged from 1K to 128K — a 128X increase — while maintaining or improving accuracy.

The practical impact is enormous: reducing training time from 12 hours to 10 minutes means CTR models can be retrained much more frequently, incorporating fresher data and responding更快 to changing user behavior. For ad systems that retrain daily (or more frequently), this translates to faster iteration cycles and more up-to-date models.

The 0.1% AUC improvement is a bonus — larger batch sizes can actually improve model quality by providing more stable gradient estimates. This challenges the common assumption that larger batch sizes sacrifice accuracy for speed.

For practitioners, CowClip offers a simple, plug-and-play technique for accelerating CTR model training. The code is open-sourced at ByteDance's LargeBatchCTR repository, making it easy to apply to existing training pipelines. The key insight — that embedding layers require different scaling rules than dense layers — is applicable to any model with sparse feature embeddings.

Sources:

  • https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.06240

item.title: AHBid: Adaptable Hierarchical Bidding with 13.57% Return Increase via Diffusion Models (WWW 2026)
item.description:
Researchers published AHBid (Adaptable Hierarchical Bidding Framework), which uses diffusion models for budget allocation in cross-channel advertising. Online A/B testing showed a 13.57% increase in overall return compared to existing baselines. The paper was accepted at WWW 2026.

AHBid addresses limitations of existing approaches for multi-channel ad bidding. Optimization-based methods lack flexibility in adapting to dynamic market conditions, while reinforcement learning approaches often struggle to capture essential historical dependencies within MDP frameworks. Cross-channel scenarios are particularly challenging because each channel has distinct behavioral patterns.

The architecture integrates two key layers:

  • High-Level Generative Planner: Uses diffusion models to dynamically allocate budgets and constraints by effectively capturing historical context and temporal patterns. Diffusion models are particularly suited for this because they can model complex, multi-modal distributions over budget allocation strategies.
  • Control-Based Bidding Algorithm: Combines historical knowledge with real-time information for improved adaptability and efficacy. This handles the day-to-day bidding decisions within the budget allocated by the planner.

Two key mechanisms ensure robustness: a Constraint Enforcement Mechanism that ensures compliance with specified constraints during bidding, and a Trajectory Refinement Mechanism that enhances adaptability to environmental changes through the utilization of historical data.

The 13.57% return increase is substantial. In advertising, return refers to the total value generated from ad spend — a 13.57% improvement means advertisers get significantly more value from the same budget, or the platform generates more revenue from the same ad inventory.

The use of diffusion models for budget planning is a novel application of generative AI to ad bidding. While diffusion models have been widely used for image and text generation, their application to sequential decision-making problems like budget allocation is relatively new. AHBid demonstrates that diffusion models can capture the complex temporal patterns in advertising data more effectively than traditional optimization or RL approaches.

For practitioners, AHBid offers a new paradigm for auto-bidding: use generative models for high-level planning and traditional algorithms for low-level execution. This hierarchical approach separates the strategic (how much to spend across channels) from the tactical (how much to bid on individual impressions) decisions.

Sources:

  • https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22650

item.title: LBM: Hierarchical Large Auto-Bidding Model via Reasoning and Acting
item.description:
Researchers published LBM (Large Auto-Bidding Model), a hierarchical model that uses LLM reasoning for automated bidding in online ad auctions. The model employs a two-level design: LBM-Think for high-level reasoning and decision-making, and LBM-Act for generating precise bidding actions.

The key innovation is the Dual Embedding Mechanism that fuses two modalities — language and numerical inputs — enabling language-guided training of the action generation module. This allows the system to leverage LLM capabilities for understanding complex auction dynamics while maintaining the numerical precision needed for competitive bidding.

To address LLM hallucinations in decision-making, LBM uses GQPO (offline reinforcement fine-tuning), a technique that enhances decision-making performance without requiring simulation or real-world rollout. This distinguishes it from prior multi-turn LLM-based approaches that require expensive environment interaction.

Existing RL and generative auto-bidding approaches can sometimes behave counterintuitively due to their black-box training manner. Direct LLM application faces difficulties with precise actions in competitive auctions and hallucination risks. LBM addresses both issues by combining structured reasoning with constrained action generation.

The hierarchical design separates strategic reasoning (what to optimize for, how to allocate budget) from tactical execution (exact bid amounts), allowing each component to specialize. LBM-Think handles the complex reasoning about auction dynamics and advertiser objectives, while LBM-Act translates those decisions into precise numerical bids.

For practitioners, LBM demonstrates that LLMs can be effectively applied to auto-bidding when properly structured. The key is not to use LLMs end-to-end for bid generation, but to use them for the reasoning component while maintaining traditional approaches for numerical precision. The dual embedding mechanism and GPO training technique offer practical solutions to the hallucination and precision challenges that arise when applying LLMs to numerical decision-making tasks.

Sources:

  • https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.05134

item.title: DARA: Few-Shot Budget Allocation with RL-Finetuned LLMs for Online Advertising (WWW 2026)
item.description:
Researchers published DARA, a framework for few-shot budget allocation in online advertising using RL-finetuned LLMs. The approach consistently outperforms existing baselines in terms of cumulative advertiser value under budget constraints. The paper was accepted at WWW 2026.

DARA addresses the AI-Generated Bidding (AIGB) paradigm, where advertisers have personalized objectives but limited historical interaction data. Traditional RL methods struggle in these few-shot scenarios because they require extensive environment interaction to learn effective policies.

The framework uses a dual-phase approach:

  • Few-shot Reasoner: Generates initial plans via in-context prompting, leveraging LLM in-context learning from limited data. This captures the LLM's ability to reason about novel situations from few examples.
  • Fine-grained Optimizer: Refines these plans using feedback-driven reasoning, providing the numerical precision needed for competitive bidding.

The key technical contribution is GRPO-Adaptive, an efficient LLM post-training strategy that enhances both reasoning and numerical precision by dynamically updating the reference policy during training. This addresses LLMs' lack of numerical precision required for fine-grained optimization.

The few-shot setting is particularly important for new advertisers or new campaigns that don't have enough historical data for traditional RL methods. DARA's ability to generate reasonable bidding strategies from limited data makes it applicable to cold-start scenarios that are common in advertising platforms.

For practitioners, DARA demonstrates that LLMs can be effectively used for bidding optimization when properly fine-tuned and structured. The dual-phase approach — using LLMs for reasoning and traditional optimization for numerical refinement — is a practical pattern for applying LLMs to numerical decision-making problems in ad tech.

Sources:

  • https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.14711

item.title: GAVE: Generative Auto-Bidding with Value-Guided Explorations (NeurIPS 2024 Competition Winner)
item.description:
Researchers published GAVE (Generative Auto-bidding with Value-Guided Explorations), an offline generative auto-bidding system that won first place in the NeurIPS 2024 AIGB competition. The system outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both offline evaluations and real-world deployments.

GAVE uses a score-based Return-To-Go (RTG) Module that accommodates various advertising objectives. The RTG module allows the system to optimize for different goals (conversions, revenue, engagement) without changing the core architecture. An action exploration mechanism integrates exploration with an RTG-based evaluation method to explore novel actions while ensuring stability-preserving updates.

A key component is the learnable value function designed to guide the direction of action exploration and mitigate Out-of-Distribution (OOD) problems. OOD issues are common in offline RL because the training data may not cover all possible states and actions the system encounters during deployment.

The paper addresses limitations of existing approaches: rule-based strategies lack adaptability to time-varying market conditions, RL-based methods struggle to capture essential historical dependencies within MDP frameworks, and offline training on fixed datasets causes behavioral collapse.

GAVE uses an offline training paradigm for deploying stable online strategies, built on generative models (score-based, suggesting diffusion-style generation). This allows the system to learn from historical data without the risks and costs of online experimentation.

Winning the NeurIPS 2024 AIGB competition demonstrates that GAVE's approach is state-of-the-art in the generative auto-bidding paradigm. The competition likely tested against diverse advertising scenarios and constraints, validating the system's generalization capabilities.

For practitioners, GAVE demonstrates that generative models (similar to those used for image/text generation) can be effectively applied to auto-bidding. The score-based approach allows for more flexible exploration of the action space compared to deterministic policies, potentially discovering better bidding strategies in complex auction environments.

Sources:

  • https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.14587

item.title: DiseCTR: Disentangled Interest Network for Out-of-Distribution CTR Prediction
item.description:
Researchers published DiseCTR, a disentangled interest network for out-of-distribution (OOD) CTR prediction. The model performs causal factorization of CTR prediction with three mechanisms, achieving AUC and GAUC improvements of over 0.02 and logloss reduction of over 13.7% versus state-of-the-art on three real-world datasets. The paper was accepted by ACM TOIS.

The OOD problem in CTR prediction arises because user interests are constantly evolving, and training and test data distributions differ. Users also tend to have multiple interests, some of which evolve faster than others. Traditional CTR models trained on historical data may not generalize well to changing user preferences.

DiseCTR addresses this through three causal mechanisms:

  • Interest Encoder: Uses sparse attention to map raw features to user interests, extracting the underlying interest signals from noisy behavioral data.
  • Weakly Supervised Interest Disentangler: Learns independent interest embeddings by disentangling multiple aspects of user interests. This separates fast-evolving interests from stable ones.
  • Attentive Interest Aggregator: Integrates disentangled interest embeddings for final click prediction, weighting each interest by its relevance to the candidate ad.

The key finding is that disentangling user interests is the key to OOD generalization for CTR prediction. By separating different interest components, the model can generalize better to new user behaviors because it understands which interests are stable and which are changing.

The 0.02 AUC improvement may seem small, but in CTR prediction at scale, even tiny AUC improvements translate to significant revenue gains. The 13.7% logloss reduction is more substantial and indicates that the model's probability estimates are significantly more accurate.

For practitioners, DiseCTR demonstrates that causal reasoning about user interests can improve CTR model robustness. The disentanglement approach is particularly relevant for ad systems that need to handle rapidly changing user preferences, such as during seasonal events or trending topics.

The code is released on GitHub, making it accessible for practitioners who want to apply these techniques to their own CTR prediction systems.

item.title: MEC: 50X Embedding Compression for CTR Prediction via Popularity-Weighted Quantization (DASFAA 2025)
item.description:
Researchers published MEC (Model-agnostic Embedding Compression), a framework that achieves over 50X memory reduction in embedding tables while maintaining or improving recommendation performance. The paper was accepted at DASFAA 2025.

Embedding tables in CTR prediction models can become excessively large, surpassing GPU memory limits. MEC addresses this through a two-stage approach:

  • Popularity-weighted regularization: Balances code distribution between high- and low-frequency features, ensuring that popular and rare features receive appropriate representation in the compressed space. This prevents the common problem where rare features get squeezed out during compression.
  • Contrastive learning mechanism: Ensures a uniform distribution of quantized codes, enhancing the distinctiveness of embeddings. This prevents the compressed embeddings from collapsing into similar representations.

The core technique is quantization of pre-trained embeddings, and the framework is model-agnostic — it can be applied across different CTR prediction architectures without modification. This means practitioners can use MEC to compress existing models without retraining from scratch.

The 50X memory reduction is transformative for production ad systems. Embedding tables often account for the majority of model parameters in CTR prediction models, and their size directly impacts serving costs (GPU memory, network bandwidth for distributed serving). A 50X reduction means models that previously required expensive GPU servers could potentially serve on much cheaper hardware.

The fact that recommendation performance is maintained or improving is crucial — compression techniques that sacrifice accuracy are not viable in production ad systems where even small accuracy drops translate to significant revenue losses.

For practitioners, MEC offers a practical solution to the embedding table size problem that plagues large-scale CTR models. The model-agnostic nature means it can be applied as a post-training optimization step, making it easy to integrate into existing deployment pipelines.

The code is available on GitHub, making it accessible for practitioners who want to apply these techniques to their own models.

Sources:

item.title: AutoDis: Automatic Discretization for Numerical Feature Embedding in CTR Prediction with 2.1% CTR Lift (KDD 2021)
item.description:
Researchers published AutoDis, a framework for embedding numerical features in CTR prediction models. Online A/B testing on an advertising platform showed +2.1% CTR and +2.7% eCPM improvement over the base model. The paper was published at KDD 2021.

Most deep CTR models follow an Embedding & Feature Interaction paradigm, but prior work focused on architecture design while the feature embedding, especially for numerical features, has been overlooked. Numerical features (like age, price, time) are typically handled by simple discretization or direct concatenation, losing important information.

AutoDis consists of three core components:

  • Meta-Embeddings: Learnable parameters per numerical field that capture global field-level knowledge with a manageable number of parameters. These provide a rich representation space for numerical values.
  • Automatic Discretization: A differentiable soft discretization module that models correlations between numerical features and meta-embeddings. Unlike hard discretization (bucketing), this preserves gradient flow for end-to-end training.
  • Aggregation Function: Combines discretized representations to produce distinctive and informative embeddings.

The framework aims for three properties: high model capacity, end-to-end training, and unique representation properties preserved. It addresses weaknesses in prior numerical feature handling, which suffered from low capacity or hard discretization based on offline expertise feature engineering.

The 2.1% CTR and 2.7% eCPM improvements demonstrate that better numerical feature handling can deliver meaningful business impact. eCPM (effective Cost Per Mille) improvement means the platform generates more revenue per thousand impressions.

For practitioners, AutoDis highlights an often-overlooked optimization opportunity: how numerical features are embedded. Most CTR model research focuses on feature interaction architectures, but the quality of input embeddings — especially for numerical features — is equally important. AutoDis offers a principled, learnable approach to numerical feature embedding that outperforms manual discretization strategies.

The code is open-sourced in MindSpore, making it accessible for practitioners who want to improve their numerical feature handling.

item.title: FINT: Field-Aware Interaction Neural Network with 2.72% Ad Revenue Lift (ICASSP 2022)
item.description:
Researchers published FINT (Field-aware INTeraction Neural Network) for CTR prediction. In production A/B testing on a big online video app, FINT achieved a 2.72% increase in advertising revenue. The paper was accepted at ICASSP 2022.

FINT addresses two challenges in CTR prediction: under-explored high-order feature interactions and the neglect of semantic information from low-order fields. The core component is a Field-aware Interaction layer that captures high-order feature interactions while retaining low-order field information, without increasing computation.

Unlike existing approaches that calculate feature interactions using simple inner products or element-wise products, FINT models feature interactions with field awareness — recognizing that features from different fields (user demographics, ad attributes, context) have different semantic meanings and interaction patterns.

The model was benchmarked on three datasets (KDD2012, Criteo, Avazu) and significantly improved performance compared to existing methods across all three. The production A/B test showing 2.72% ad revenue lift validates that these offline improvements translate to real business impact.

For practitioners, FINT demonstrates that field-aware feature interaction is a simple but effective technique for improving CTR prediction models. The code is released on GitHub, making it easy to apply to existing models.

Sources:

item.title: Deep Behavior Path Matching Network for CTR Prediction at Meituan: 1.6% CTR and 1.8% Revenue Lift (WWW 2023)
item.description:
Meituan deployed the Deep Behavior Path Matching Network for CTR prediction, achieving +1.6% CTR and +1.8% advertising revenue in online A/B testing. The paper was accepted at WWW 2023.

The core concept is behavior paths — sequences of user actions that capture the cognitive clue of the user's decision-making on e-commerce apps. The model matches a user's current behavior path against historical behavior paths to predict click-through behavior.

Three key techniques address modeling challenges:

  • Contrastive Learning: Augments user behavior paths, addressing sparsity in behavioral data. This creates more training signal from limited data.
  • Behavior Path Self-Activation: Alleviates the effect of noise in behavior sequences. Not all user actions are meaningful — some are accidental or exploratory.
  • Two-Level Matching Mechanism: Identifies the most appropriate candidate among historical paths. This captures both coarse-grained patterns (overall shopping intent) and fine-grained patterns (specific product preferences).

The idea of matching behavior paths rather than individual items is novel. Traditional CTR models consider each ad in isolation, but users make decisions in the context of their current browsing session. A user searching for "running shoes" has different intent than a user casually browsing — even if they click on the same ad.

The 1.6% CTR and 1.8% revenue improvements demonstrate that behavior path matching delivers meaningful business impact. The deployment at Meituan's food delivery platform validates that these techniques work in a production environment with strict latency requirements.

For practitioners, this work highlights the importance of session-level context in CTR prediction. Modeling the user's current behavior path — not just individual actions — can capture intent signals that pointwise models miss.

Sources:

item.title: DCIN: Deep Context Interest Network with 1.5% CTR and 1.5% RPM Lift at Online Advertising System (CIKM 2023)
item.description:
Researchers deployed DCIN (Deep Context Interest Network) for CTR prediction, jointly modeling user clicks and their surrounding display context. Online deployment on a production advertising system showed +1.5% CTR and +1.5% RPM improvements. The paper was accepted at CIKM 2023.

Most existing user behavior modeling approaches only model users' positive interests from clicked items while ignoring the context information — the display items shown alongside the clicked items. DCIN addresses this by incorporating context information into user interest modeling.

The architecture has three core modules:

  • Position-aware Context Aggregation Module (PCAM): Aggregates display items using an attention mechanism, incorporating positional information about items relative to the click. Items shown near the clicked item provide signal about what caught the user's attention.
  • Feedback-Context Fusion Module (FCFM): Combines click representations with display context representations through non-linear feature interaction. This captures the relationship between what the user clicked and what else was visible.
  • Interest Matching Module (IMM): Activates interests related with the target item, effectively performing interest-target relevance scoring.

The key insight is that clicking behavior is influenced by context — a user might click an ad because it was the best option among the displayed items, not because it perfectly matches their interest. Understanding this context helps the model make better predictions about future clicks.

The 1.5% CTR and RPM improvements demonstrate that context-aware modeling delivers meaningful business impact. The paper includes a hands-on solution for implementing DCIN on large-scale industrial systems, making it practical for production deployment.

For practitioners, DCIN highlights the importance of display context in CTR prediction. Modeling what else the user saw when they clicked — not just what they clicked — can capture important signals about user intent and ad quality.

Sources:

item.title: LCN: Cross-Domain LifeLong Sequential Modeling for CTR Prediction at WeChat (KDD 2024)
item.description:
WeChat deployed LCN (Lifelong Cross Network) for cross-domain CTR prediction, incorporating user behavior sequences from both target and source domains. The model outperforms existing work in terms of both prediction accuracy and online performance. The paper was accepted at KDD 2024.

LCN addresses the challenge of cross-domain lifelong sequential modeling (LSM), where user behavior sequences from multiple domains (e.g., different products or services within WeChat) need to be leveraged for CTR prediction. Previous work focused on domain-specific LSM, but limited work had been done on cross-domain approaches.

The model has two key components:

  • LifeLong Attention Pyramid (LAP): Comprises three levels of cascaded attentions to effectively extract interest representations from lifelong sequences with respect to candidate items. The pyramid structure captures both fine-grained recent interests and coarse-grained long-term preferences.
  • Cross Representation Production (CRP): Enforces additional supervision on the learning and alignment of cross-domain representations so they transfer better to the target domain's CTR task. This prevents negative transfer where source domain knowledge hurts target domain performance.

The deployment at WeChat Channels — a short video platform with hundreds of millions of users — validates that cross-domain lifelong sequential modeling works at massive scale. The ability to leverage user behavior from one domain (e.g., WeChat messaging) to improve CTR prediction in another domain (e.g., WeChat Channels ads) is valuable because it provides richer user modeling even for users with limited activity in the target domain.

For practitioners, LCN demonstrates that cross-domain user behavior modeling can deliver improvements over domain-specific approaches. The key challenges are in the alignment — how to make representations from different domains compatible — and the supervision — how to prevent negative transfer. LCN's LifeLong Attention Pyramid and Cross Representation Production offer practical solutions to these challenges.

Sources:
